trades.headline: Trade from deep RB (James Cook, Tank Dell) for buy-low Justin Jefferson while backup Carson Wentz is at QB.
trades.summary: Jefferson is being blanketed by top corners behind a backup quarterback while Kyler Murray recovers from a hamstring strain - a dated, fixable cause, not a lost role. James Cook, a strength you can spare, and a throwaway Tank Dell fund it.

give: You already start three running backs (Bijan Robinson, James Cook, Quinshon Judkins); Cook is replaceable depth, not a hole.
Cook is still productive, not declining - 22 carries for 95 yards and a touchdown as recently as Week 6 - so you're selling strength, not papering over a slump.
Tank Dell is a 40% snap-share complementary piece as he works back from missing all of 2025 with a knee injury; his value spike is a sugar high from one 63-yard touchdown.
get: Jefferson managed just 2 catches on 10 targets for 39 yards in a 23-6 loss to Buffalo, shadowed most of the game by top corner Christian Benford - rough results, but he still drew 10 looks.

Kyler Murray strained his hamstring in Week 8 and has missed games since, forcing backup Carson Wentz (8-of-25, 81 yards, 3 turnovers that same Buffalo game) into the lineup - the Vikings are targeting Murray's return in Week 12, a dated recovery, not a permanent downgrade.
Omarion Hampton is a throw-in with his own name-brand upside if the Chargers' backfield consolidates.
you: Jefferson slots straight into your starting WR spot in place of a cold DK Metcalf, finally addressing your thin receiver corps.

Hampton projects to win a flex spot on raw points once he's in the building, but his role has reportedly been shrinking in Los Angeles - treat him as a bench piece you can sit anytime, not a lineup cornerstone.
them: Bishop Schlottamore is deep at WR/TE already, so moving Jefferson for a clear running back upgrade (Cook) fills their thin backfield.
Dell is a low-cost throw-in they can stash while he builds back toward a full role.
experts: Jefferson finished 2-for-39 on 10 targets as Buffalo improved to 7-1 with a 23-6 win on Nov. 9, 2026, with Christian Benford shadowing him most of the game.
Kyler Murray strained his hamstring in Minnesota's Week 8 loss to Detroit and has missed every game since; the team is targeting his return for Week 12 against Atlanta on Nov. 29.
Cook remains part of a heavy Buffalo workload into November, including a 95-yard, one-score Week 6 game against the Raiders.

risks: If Murray's hamstring lingers past the Week 12 target, Jefferson's price stays depressed longer than you'd like.
Hampton's role has reportedly been shrinking behind a hot-hand rotation in the Chargers' backfield - treat him as a lottery ticket, not a sure thing.

trades.headline: Cash in Stefon Diggs off his Thursday-night walk-off for an injured, buy-low Josh Jacobs.
trades.summary: Diggs just delivered the game-winning touchdown on Thursday Night Football, the kind of moment that inflates a sell-high price. Jacobs is cheap only because he fractured a finger in Week 9 - a short-term issue, not a lost job.

give: Diggs caught a 32-yard, game-winning touchdown from Jayden Daniels with 57 seconds left to beat the Giants 24-21 on Thursday night - his price won't be higher than right after a moment like that.
Diggs's FantasyCalc value is up 73% over 30 days and he's scoring 1.26x his own projection - a hot stretch at age 32, not a durable role change.
You already start three running backs; Judkins is surplus depth, especially since Cleveland splits his touches with Dylan Sampson.
get: Josh Jacobs fractured his right ring finger on November 8 against the Patriots, needs surgery, and is expected to miss just 2-3 weeks - a short, specific absence, not a lost job.
Jakobi Meyers is a cheap complementary throw-in.
you: Removing Diggs promotes Tank Dell, already on your bench, straight into a starting flex spot.
Jacobs takes over Judkins's roster spot and is ready to start again once his finger heals in a few weeks.
them: Beautiful -> is 2-8 and thin at WR/TE; Diggs is a proven, surging target they need now.
With Jacobs expected back in 2-3 weeks, they give up little short-term production for immediate receiver help.
experts: Diggs's Thursday-night, game-winning touchdown catch came in Washington's 24-21 win over the Giants on November 12, 2026, resetting his price near a season high.
Jacobs needs surgery on a fractured right ring finger suffered in Week 9 against New England and is expected back in 2-3 weeks, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport (NBC Sports, Nov. 11, 2026).

risks: If Jacobs's finger recovery drags past 3 weeks, or Chris Brooks keeps the third-down role when Jacobs returns, this buy-low takes longer to pay off.
Diggs leaned on a walk-off moment for this price; if Washington's offense cools off, his value gain may not hold.

trades.headline: Turn a crowded RB bench (James Cook) into two buy-low WR1s: Chris Olave and Zay Flowers.
trades.summary: Flowers keeps his full featured role despite a depressed price, fresh off a $140 million extension. Olave is a riskier half of the deal - rookie Jordyn Tyson is cutting into his targets - but your running back room can easily absorb losing Cook either way.

give: You roster three running backs (Bijan Robinson, Cook, Judkins); moving Cook costs you no lineup spot.
Cook remains productive - 95 yards and a touchdown as recently as Week 6 - so you're selling a strength, not covering for a decline.
get: Chris Olave is still Tyler Shough's WR2 and his FantasyCalc value is down 15% over 30 days, but rookie Jordyn Tyson is a real and growing threat to his target share, not just an injured name on IR.
Zay Flowers signed a four-year, $140 million extension in August, cementing his role (69% snap share, 28% target share) even as his price slid 31% over 30 days.
you: Olave and Flowers both start immediately in place of Cook and a cold DK Metcalf, addressing your thin receiver corps with two players at once.
them: Charity Case is 3-7, thin at QB/WR and deep at RB/TE - they fill a real backfield need with Cook and move two receivers they can spare.
experts: Olave drew a season-low 4 targets (3 catches, 30 yards) in a 20-17 Week 10 loss to Carolina, while rookie Jordyn Tyson - back from a hamstring injury that cost him the first eight weeks - jumped to a team-high 13 targets that same game; Olave is still graded a WR2 heading into Week 11 (Rotoballer, Nov. 15, 2026).
Flowers signed a four-year, $140 million extension in August 2026, confirming Baltimore's long-term investment in his role even after an earlier hamstring scare.

risks: Jordyn Tyson's emergence (team-high 13 targets in Week 10) is the real threat here - if he keeps that role, Olave's price may not recover much even once Shough settles in.
Flowers has dealt with a hamstring issue this year; a recurrence would keep this buy-low cheap longer than hoped.

trades.headline: Sell Trevor Lawrence at his career-high price for Brock Purdy plus a buy-low Rhamondre Stevenson.
trades.summary: Lawrence's trade value is up 54% in 30 days while his per-game output merely matches his own season-long projection - this is the moment to sell. Purdy is a stable low-end QB1, and Stevenson is a cheap flier.

give: Trevor Lawrence's FantasyCalc value has risen 54% over the last 30 days on a breakout-quarterback narrative.
His 20.3 points per game sits right at his own season-long projection (0.97 perf) - that's reputation driving the price, not a hot streak outproducing his role.
Malik Washington is buried on your bench behind five receivers already ahead of him.
get: Brock Purdy starts for a run-first 49ers offense built around Christian McCaffrey and George Kittle, a stable low-end QB1 floor.
Rhamondre Stevenson's FantasyCalc value is down over the last 30 days even though he's still New England's change-of-pace back.
you: Purdy steps directly into your starting QB spot in place of Lawrence.
Stevenson's touches project ahead of a cold DK Metcalf for your second flex spot, even though you're already deep at running back overall.
them: 2x Champ Killer Corgis are thin at RB and TE; Stevenson's touches address a real hole even as a committee piece.
Lawrence is a clear quarterback upgrade for a team deep enough at the position to move Purdy without blinking.
experts: Jacksonville beat Tennessee 40-23 in Week 10, extending the Jaguars' surge and the 'generational quarterback' narrative driving Lawrence's FantasyCalc spike.
Purdy enters the week as San Francisco's starter after missing time last season to shoulder and toe injuries, with analysts still pegging him as a low-end QB1 given the 49ers' weapons.

risks: If Lawrence's hot stretch continues into the fantasy playoffs, this looks like selling too early.
Stevenson is clearly a committee piece in New England, not a workhorse.
This and the Jared Goff deal both sell Lawrence - you can only make one; pick whichever partner's return you value more.

trades.headline: A second way to sell Trevor Lawrence's peak price: a reliable Jared Goff plus a depth flier in Kyren Williams.
trades.summary: Same sell-high logic as the Purdy deal, aimed at a different partner: Lawrence's trade value is inflated by narrative more than weekly output, and Goff is a steady top-10 fantasy quarterback. Williams is a lower-confidence add given Los Angeles's crowded backfield.

give: Trevor Lawrence's FantasyCalc value is up 54% over 30 days on reputation, not weekly outproduction - his 0.97 perf means he's matching his own already-elevated projection, not beating it.
You only need one of your two playable quarterbacks (Lawrence, Jayden Daniels); moving the more inflated one locks in the gain.
get: Jared Goff finished a third straight season as a top-10 fantasy quarterback in 2025 and projects for another full, healthy slate in 2026, a steady floor to replace Lawrence.
Kyren Williams is a name-value flier - still part of the Rams' backfield even as Blake Corum eats into his workload.
you: Goff steps directly into your starting QB spot.
Williams's touches edge out a cold DK Metcalf for your second flex, even though you're already deep at running back.
them: Garbage Time Goblins are 7-3 and thin at QB/TE - Lawrence is a clear starting upgrade for a team pushing for the playoffs, and they're deep enough at RB/WR to deal from Williams.
experts: Goff ranked second in the NFL in both passing yards and touchdowns in 2025, his third straight top-10 fantasy finish, with analysts projecting another strong season in 2026.
Williams's workload is reportedly shrinking as Sean McVay leans more on Blake Corum, with one 2026 outlook projecting his touches falling from 300+ last season to roughly 200-250.

risks: Williams is the riskiest piece here - if the Corum committee deepens further, he may not be worth a starting spot even in your deep RB room.
This and the Brock Purdy deal both sell Lawrence - you can only make one; pick whichever partner's return you value more.

notes: Rewrote the Justin Jefferson trade (mrwbnw): the original claim that Minnesota signed Kirk Cousins this week was wrong. Corrected to the real cause of Jefferson's slump - Kyler Murray's hamstring strain (since Week 8) forcing backup Carson Wentz into the lineup, with Murray targeting a Week 12 return. Also fixed a lineup-claim mismatch: Omarion Hampton actually projects to start, not sit on the bench, so reworded to flag his shrinking role as a real risk instead of calling him a safe bench stash. Lowered confidence to medium.

Fixed the Chris Olave half of the Olave/Flowers trade (12e41v7): rookie Jordyn Tyson is not injured and sidelined as originally written - he's active and took a team-high 13 targets in Week 10 while Olave fell to a season-low 4. Reworded to present Tyson's emergence as a genuine, ongoing threat to Olave's role rather than dismissing him, and lowered confidence to medium.
Verified the Diggs/Jacobs, Lawrence/Purdy and Lawrence/Goff trades against fresh sources; no factual corrections needed there.
